data.description:
## testing_mode: GREEN

Add a test verifying cited_lines is preserved through the overlay merge logic in ci-llm-review-runner.sh.

## Files to Modify
- tests/scripts/test-ci-llm-review-runner.sh

## Acceptance Criteria

### Before implementing:
Read tests/scripts/test-ci-llm-review-runner.sh to identify the existing overlay merge test pattern (tests around lines 1319-1333 cover security/performance/test-quality overlay merges). Follow that exact pattern.

### Test to add: test_overlay_merge_preserves_cited_lines

Given:
- Tier findings JSON: one finding with cited_lines: ["main.sh:10"], severity: "minor", category: "hygiene", description: "test", file: "main.sh"
- Overlay findings JSON: one finding with cited_lines: ["util.sh:25"], severity: "minor", category: "correctness", description: "test", file: "util.sh"

When: the overlay merge Python logic is exercised (follow existing test pattern for invoking this logic)

Then: the merged output contains both findings and each retains its cited_lines value unchanged

**IMPORTANT: ALL fixture findings MUST include cited_lines so this test stays green after T7 activates the gate.**

### Implementation note:
The existing overlay merge tests use a mock write-reviewer-findings.sh that bypasses schema validation — this is by design. Those existing tests are safe after T7 because the mock skips the real validator. The new T5 test verifies cited_lines pass-through behavior (not full schema validity). This test passes immediately since ci-llm-review-runner.sh's overlay merge uses:
  merged_findings.extend(overlay.get('findings', []))
which copies the complete finding dict including cited_lines.
data.title: T5: Write overlay merge cited_lines pass-through test in test-ci-llm-review-runner.sh
